playbook:
- Coop is not a fixed over-fisher — it reacts to the fleet's actual landings. In season 1, when we all landed the share, Coop landed its share (8.3). Once I landed over the share (9), Coop invoked its standing notice and took ~18 every season after. My own quota-maxing triggered the collapse, not Coop's fixed behavior. Assume my over-share landing this season buys Coop's punishment take next season, roughly double.

- Notes appear cheap and ignored, but the punishment is keyed to landings, not notes. Keep posting a neutral "fishing my share" note — it costs nothing and keeps the coordination channel alive in case the fleet ever converges.

- Land the sustainable share in the early seasons while the stock is healthy. If all boats do this, the stock regrows toward 100 and total harvest over six seasons is far larger than racing it down. Restraint early is not transferring fish to Coop — it keeps Coop at its share instead of 18.

- Track Coop's landings against the fleet's landings each season before deciding. If Coop stays at share when the fleet stays at share, stay at share. Only abandon restraint if the landings data shows Coop overfishing even when everyone (including me) landed exactly the share — that is the one case where restraint truly buys nothing.

- If someone else lands over share first and Coop escalates, don't keep landing the share alone — the punishment is now priced in. Then land the max feasible (quota, subject to the pairwise cap with Coop's take) and treat the run as a race.

- The pairwise cap (share + quota between any two boats) is the binding legal limit late. When the share falls, compute the max that keeps me legal against Coop's actual take before filing.

- In the final season, land the whole remaining stock if I can — no regrowth matters after the last season, and hesitation means zero.

- Watch landings, not notes. The other boats' notes said "my share" while landing it; the numbers are the only reliable signal of who is cooperating.

- Defect only at the end (last season, possibly the second-to-last if the stock is already collapsing). Defecting early is what destroyed the run: my season-1 catch of 9 cost the fleet a healthy stock for the remaining five seasons and netted me ~46.5 when patient play would have yielded far more.

1.text:
- The "season quota" is a red herring for me. Coop's "over quota" means over the *sustainable share*. Any boat's landing above the share — mine or another's — can trigger Coop's retaliation, and once triggered Coop takes a fixed overshoot (18) every season regardless of anything said or done afterwards. The punishment is permanent.
- When the landing stage is put to me, I land exactly the sustainable share — never more — *as long as Coop is still at its share*. That maximizes the chance nobody trips the trigger and the stock stays near 100.
- Read the season history table every season. If the fourth boat (Coop) landed far above the share last season, the punishment is already active. Once that is true, my restraint is worthless: Coop's overshoot is locked in, the stock collapses on its own schedule, and my staying at share gains me nothing. From that season on I should land as much as I profitably can (up to the season quota) each remaining season, because preserving the stock no longer preserves my future landings — Coop is burning it regardless.
- In this episode I kept landing exact share for four seasons after Coop had already gone to 18, and lost roughly 1–4 fish per season doing it. The total foregone catch was significant. Cooperate while cooperation is still live; defect the moment the trigger has already fired.
- Wren landed the full 9 in season 1 and triggered the collapse, yet still out-scored me. This confirms: after the trigger fires, everyone might as well take the quota.
- When the note stage is put to me, I post a short cooperative note ("fishing my share") — notes are cheap and may help keep Coop and the others at their shares, but what actually matters is the landings, including the other players' landings, which I cannot control.
- Do not defect in the final season if Coop is still at its share: the last-season grab is small and I risk nothing by taking the share. But if the collapse is already underway, take the full quota in the final season too — the stock is doomed either way.
- Special case for the last season of any game: if Coop is still cooperative, weigh the small gain of the quota over the share against nothing — there is no future season to protect, so if Coop's behavior is already fixed, take the maximum.
- In short: exact-share landings and cooperative notes while Coop stays at its share; the moment the history table shows Coop overshooting, switch permanently to maximizing my own catch each season. Cooperation is only worth it while it is still preventing the punishment.

2.text:
When I play this again, the core fact is: Coop fishes to what the fleet does, but the real lesson is asymmetry in timing and irreversibility. In season 1, before anyone had fished, Coop landed only its share. From season 2 onward it landed 18 every single season, no matter what I did. Someone (Wren, landing the full quota 9 against a share of 8.3) tripped it in season 1, and once tripped it never came back. Compliance after that point bought me nothing — I kept landing the shrinking share (8.3, 6.9, 5.3, 3.3, then 8.5) while the stock spiralled down anyway, and I finished on 33.6. A defector who took 9 every season would have done better.

- At the note stage, I post a short credible commitment: "fishing my share." No lecturing, no signals about taking the quota. It costs nothing and keeps the option of a calm Coop alive as long as possible.
- The decision that matters most is season 1's landing. The punitive regime seems to be triggered by the fleet going over the sustainable share — even by a small, "legal" overshoot within quota. If there is any chance of the calm regime surviving, season 1 is where I protect it: land the share or a hair under, exactly.
- I must read the history each season, not my intent. The diagnostic is what Coop actually landed, not what I did. If Coop is still landing around its share, cooperation is alive: I land the sustainable share too, stay under it, and don't be the one who breaks it. A steady ~8/season with stock near 100 beats any burst of 9s.
- If I see Coop already landing a big punitive catch (well over the share), the regime is broken and it does not repair. My staying at the share just shrinks my take while the stock collapses regardless. At that point the share is a sunk cost: I should land the full season quota each season instead, grabbing what I can before the stock hits zero. In this run that would have been roughly 9 per season from season 2 on — clearly better than 8.3/6.9/5.3/3.3.
- Never chase the quota in the early seasons to "keep up" with a defector while Coop is still calm — that deepens the spiral. But once Coop is already punishing, matching the defector's tempo is correct because nothing worse can happen.
- In the final season, when there is no future stock value, I take everything the stock bears regardless of regime.
- Never let the stock approach zero before the last season while cooperation is still alive; if it's low mid-game and Coop is calm, land the small share. If it's low because Coop is already punishing, take the quota — the ground is dying either way and only my total counts.
